title: A Caricature of Marxism and Imperialist Economism
author: V.I. Lenin
shortDescription: Lenin's polemic against 'imperialist economism', refuting the dogma that finance capital makes democratic demands, national self-determination, and anti-colonial liberation impossible or obsolete.
subject: Imperialism and National Self-Determination
context: Written between August and October 1916 in response to an article by P. Kievsky (Yuri Pyatakov), this work defended the Bolshevik position on the right of nations to self-determination against a trend among young Bolsheviks and European leftists who argued that global imperialism rendered national struggles obsolete.
relatesToToday: Directly refutes modern left-reductionist arguments that dismiss anti-colonial liberation, national sovereignty struggles in the Global South, or democratic rights as pointless distractions from pure class conflict, showing why socialism requires championing democratic self-determination.
keyTakeaways: Critique of imperialist economism: Mechanistic Marxists wrongly assumed that because finance capital rules globally, political independence and self-determination for oppressed nations are economically unachievable illusions.

Self-determination is a political, not economic, demand: Political borders and state independence can and do change under capitalism (as seen in Norway in 1905), even while economic financial ties remain.

Defense of the fatherland in just national wars: While defending the fatherland in an imperialist war between oppressor nations is chauvinist treachery, defending an oppressed nation against foreign imperialist subjugation is progressive and legitimate.

Global revolution as an epoch of combined struggles: Socialist revolution is not a simultaneous strike across all countries, but an epoch combining working-class civil war in imperialist centers with anti-colonial national liberation revolts in the periphery.

Diverse paths to socialism: While all nations will inevitably arrive at socialism, each will contribute unique forms of democracy, specific varieties of workers' power, and varying rates of transformation.
